title: Cap. VIII: Ex vs.17 — death reigns from Adam's fall; Garissoles' pervading-penalty syllogism
pass_a_gloss: Placeus opens the next head: so we come to verse 17. Garissoles (D. G.) claims that from this verse an argument like the earlier ones rises. The major runs: whoever is such that by his offense and fall death has always reigned and will reign to the age's end — that person's offense brings a penalty that spreads through everyone. Support: the Apostle treats death as the effect of that cause. The minor: by Adam's one offense death has already reigned over everyone up to now, and will keep reigning through to the age's end. Conclusion Garissoles wants: therefore the penalty of Adam's offense and fall spreads through everyone.
pass_b_english: IV. Let us come, then, to verse 17. From it, says D. Garissoles, a similar argument arises. The one by whose offense and fall death has always reigned and will reign to the end of the age — that one's offense-penalty pervades all. For death is certainly set by the Apostle as the effect of that cause (Romans 5:17). But by one offense of Adam death has so far reigned over all, and will go on reigning to the end of the age. Therefore the penalty of that offense and fall of Adam pervades all.
source_text: IV. Veniamus igitur ad verf. 17. Ex eo simile, inquit D. G. argumentum emergit. Cuius delicto & lapsu mors semper regnavit & regnatura est in finem seculi, eius delicti poena pervadit in omnes. Mors enim certe ab Apostolo ponitur, tanquam causae illius effectum. At uno Adami delicto mors hactenus in omnes regnavit, & porro regnatura est usque ad finem seculi. Igitur delicti & lapsus illius Adae poena in omnes pervagatur.
